Perfect. Now let me compile my findings into a comprehensive report.

---

## COMPREHENSIVE INKOS STATE REPORT

### SECTION A — LESSONS & ANTIPATTERNS (Ranked by Impact)

**Critical antipatterns to avoid in expansion:**

1. **Hand-edited `lib/supabase/types.ts` — THE #1 bug source** — 30+ bugs across 13 sprints traced to types not matching migrations. **Fix:** Use `pnpm supabase gen types typescript` after EVERY migration, never hand-edit (file path: `/lib/supabase/types.ts`).

2. **RPC parameter mismatches (Dato ↔ Koda drift)** — Sprint 5, 6, 7, 8 all had parameter name mismatches (`submissionId` vs `submission_id`, `public_get_invite_by_token` vs `get_invite_by_token`). **Fix:** Define RPC contracts as TypeScript interfaces IN the design spec before Dato writes SQL.

3. **`asChild` on base-nova components — Radix habit carryover** — base-ui requires `render` prop, never `asChild`. Add to ESLint config.

4. **Missing rate limits on GET endpoints** — Sprints 1, 6, 8-12. Every API route (GET or POST) must call `authedRatelimit` or `publicBookingReadRatelimit` before DB queries. Sage scan catches this.

5. **Batch audits worse than per-sprint audits** — Sprints 8-12 batched audit found 4 CRITICAL issues that had compounded for 5 sprints. **Rule:** Sage audit after EVERY sprint.

6. **Public routes using session client instead of anon** — Sprint 5 (C6, C7). All `/book/`, `/consent/`, `/invite/`, `/api/public/` routes must use `createPublicClient()` from `@/lib/supabase/public`.

7. **`unstable_cache` capturing authenticated clients** — Sprint 7 (M3). Never wrap `supabase.rpc()` in `unstable_cache` — JWT leaks across requests. Cache the RESULT, not the invocation.

8. **Dodo webhook spec: `standardwebhooks` NOT plain HMAC** — Sprint 4 (C1). Signature format: `v1,base64sig` header with `standardwebhooks.Webhook.verify()`. Never `createHmac('sha256')`.

9. **Feature gate key mismatches** — Sprint 7 (C1). Create `lib/billing/feature-keys.ts` with all gate keys as a constant; both migration seeding and `requireFeature()` callers import from it.

10. **Stub RPCs must match final signature** — Sprint 2's `public_get_availability` RPC was stubbed then replaced; shape change broke silent downstream. Stubs must return exact final shape, even if empty.

**See file:** `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md` (sections 1-7 for full detail, lines 1-300+).

---

### SECTION B — SPRINT 0-12 DELIVERED SCOPE

| Sprint | Scope |
|--------|-------|
| **S0** | Auth, RLS, user roles, multi-tenant foundation |
| **S1** | Clients CRM, contact info, tags, health checks |
| **S2** | Bookings, public availability RPC, calendar read-only |
| **S3** | Consents, form templates, audit trail, CSV export |
| **S4** | Billing (Dodo), plans, subscriptions, paywall enforcement |
| **S5** | Consent public flow, SMS reminders, Twilio integration |
| **S6** | Team members, roles, invites, member permissions |
| **S7** | Commission tracking, session accounting, splits |

#### **THE MONEY (3 modules)**

**11. Payments**
- 🟡 **PARTIAL** — Dodo Payments destination charges wired (NOT Stripe Connect per CLAUDE.md). Deposit pool draw + new charge combined at session settlement. Commission splits (configurable %). Tip routing (default 100% artist). Tax sub-ledger per location. **Missing:** dispute defense pack auto-bundling, refund flow with proportional commission reversal, Stripe Connect payout splits (uses Dodo only), 1099-NEC export (1099-K exists, 1099-NEC not found), pricing models only partially (hourly/per-piece exist, half-day/full-day/project-flat/walk-in-min not in schema).

**12. Inventory (Studio+)**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — Ink batches by manufacturer/lot/color/REACH-MoCRA status. Gloves/needles/Saniderm tracking (low-stock alerts + BullMQ trigger). REACH compliance log per batch. Routes: `/inventory`, `/inventory/stocktake`. Inventory KPI RPC wired for analytics.

**13. Analytics (Studio+)**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — 6 report tabs: Revenue (timeline, KPIs, CSV), Artists (leaderboard), Clients (LTV, retention 30/90/365), Bookings (heatmap, timeline), Inventory (COGS, categories), AI Usage (cost, model breakdown). Routes: `/reports/{revenue,artists,clients,bookings,inventory,ai}`. Realtime data from RPCs. **Note:** Named `/reports` in codebase, not `/analytics` per PDF.

---

#### **INTELLIGENCE (2 modules)**

**14. Marketing (Studio+)**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — Automated flows: win-back (6-month), loyalty (points + tier credits), birthday cards (day-14 after project), review capture (Google + IG). Visual editor for emails/SMS exists (basic form UI, not drag-drop). Segment builder from Analytics data wired. Routes: `/marketing`, `/marketing/campaigns/new`.

**15. AI Assist (Pro+)**
- 🟡 **PARTIAL** — (1) Inbound reply drafts NOT implemented (conceptual in spec only). (2) Session-to-notes summarization NOT found. (3) Auto-generate aftercare from session data NOT implemented. What exists: Claude vision auto-tagger for flash pieces (`/api/ai/flash-tag`), design moodboard + reference search (`/ai-design` routes). No "never sends autonomously" guard found for drafts. **High gap risk.**

**16. Settings**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — Studio identity, hours, locations, tax rates per location, commission templates, payout schedules, cancellation policies (3-tier: >48h, 24-48h, <24h). Deposit rules, kiosk iPad config, booking widget customization. Integrations: Stripe Connect (payment method only, not payouts), Meta (Instagram/Messenger webhooks), WhatsApp (Twilio), Twilio (SMS), Resend (email). GDPR/CCPA retention settings (data deletion RPC exists). Audit log. Routes: `/settings/**` including `/settings/ink-registry`.

---

### CRITICAL GAPS

**Architecture & Entity Gaps**
- ✅ Deposit pool entity EXISTS as first-class (4 columns: in_cents, applied_cents, available_cents, refundable_cents on `projects` table + deposit_transactions child table + auto-apply RPC).
- ✅ Unified inbox EXISTS (omnichannel_inbox feature gate, `/messages` page, conversation + client_communications schema).
- ❌ **Stripe Connect marketplace payouts NOT built** — only Dodo Payments for destination charges. Commission splits via config, not via Connect account payouts. This is an intentional architectural choice (CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids Stripe, mandates Dodo).
- ❌ **Kiosk mode PARTIALLY wired** — `/forms/kiosk` exists for consent signing on iPad, but full pre-session briefing kiosk (phone lookup → 3 forms → hash + timestamp) incomplete. Consent kiosk sessions table exists but form auto-fill from client notes/allergies/deposits not integrated.
- ❌ **Client portal via SMS magic link NOT found** — project view, deposit pool, photo timeline, consent read-only portal not in `/api/` or app routes. Consent forms have magic links, but no dedicated client portal page.
- ❌ **AI Assist drafts for inbound replies NOT built** — only design assistant exists.
- ❌ **Persistent allergies banner across all client tabs NOT wired** — allergies column exists on `clients`, but no persistent banner component visible in client detail layout.
- ❌ **30-minute pre-session briefing push NOT automated** — no worker job or API endpoint collating allergies + notes + last 3 sessions + deposits + outstanding forms.

**Data Model Gaps**
- ✅ Core tables exist: studios, users (with artist_type, commission_model, tax info), bookings, sessions, projects, clients, deposits/deposit_pool, payments, photos, notes, forms, consent, inventory, ink_batches, marketing_campaigns.
- ❌ **Photo timeline slots schema INCOMPLETE** — `project_progress_photos` has slot_type (before_skin, reference, s{N}_fresh, s{N}_healed) and session_number, due_date, privacy columns (added in latest migration 20260430100000), but no "session" as a separate bookings link. Session completion triggered by booking status change (trigger exists), but no explicit `sessions` table — projects infer sessions from bookings.
- ❌ **1099-NEC export NOT found** — only 1099-K. Tax sub-ledger exists (audit-logged) but no NEC export RPC.
- ❌ **Dispute defense pack table NOT found** — no schema for auto-bundling refund defense docs.

**Integration Gaps**
- ✅ Instagram/Messenger webhook EXISTS (Meta API, channel-mapped to conversations).
- ✅ WhatsApp webhook EXISTS (Twilio, channel-mapped to conversations).
- ✅ Twilio SMS webhook EXISTS (channel-mapped to conversations).
- ✅ Email webhook EXISTS (Resend inbound, channel-mapped to conversations).
- ❌ **Stripe Connect NOT wired** — forbidden by architecture (Dodo only).
- ❌ **Mailchimp integration NOT found** — no segment export or sync flow.
- ⚠️ **Meta (Instagram/Messenger) webhook WIRED but not fully tested** — webhook route exists (`/api/webhooks/instagram`), conversations table supports `meta_page_id` and `meta_conversation_id`, but no documented feature gate or admin test suite.

**Migration Risks**
- ⚠️ **`/reports` vs `/analytics` naming mismatch** — PDF calls it "Analytics (Studio+)", codebase routes are `/reports/`. No conflict; just naming divergence. Feature key is `analytics`.
- ⚠️ **Existing `/reports` (Sprint 12 addition) may shadow future `/analytics` module** — currently the same thing, but if they diverge, URL routing becomes ambiguous.
- ⚠️ **Legacy demo seed data** — scripts/seed/demo/README.md mentions deprecated `scripts/seed-calendar-demo.sql` + `20260501200000_inbox_demo_data.sql` scheduled for removal next sprint. Both still in repo.

---

### NOTABLE CONFLICTS

| Conflict | PDF Spec | CLAUDE.md | Resolution |
|----------|----------|-----------|-----------|
| **Payment Processor** | Stripe Connect for marketplace splits, destination charges, commission splits | Dodo Payments only (Stripe forbidden) | ✅ **RESOLVED:** Dodo is production choice. Commission splits via studio config, not Connect accounts. |
| **Analytics Module Name** | "Analytics (Studio+)" | Feature key is `analytics`, routes are `/reports` | ✅ **RESOLVED:** No functional conflict, just naming. Routes are `/reports/{revenue,artists,clients,bookings,inventory,ai}`. |
| **AI Assist Scope** | (1) Inbound reply drafts (2) Session summary (3) Aftercare generation | Current code only supports Claude vision for flash tagging + design moodboards | ❌ **UNRESOLVED:** PDF specifies 3 AI jobs, only design support exists. Drafts/summary/aftercare not implemented. Risk for launch. |
| **Public Portfolio Domain** | portfolio.inkos.studio/[studio]/[artist] | Routes at `/p/[studioSlug]/[artistSlug]` | ⚠️ **PARTIAL:** Internal routes exist, custom domain mapping not found. Public pages ARE served but via `/p/` path, not studio-branded subdomain. |

---

### CROSS-CUTTING WORKFLOWS — IMPLEMENTATION STATUS

| Workflow | Status | Notes |
|----------|--------|-------|
| 30-min pre-session briefing push | ❌ MISSING | No worker/endpoint collating allergies + notes + deposits + forms. Allergies banner not persistent in UI. |
| iPad kiosk check-in | 🟡 PARTIAL | Consent signing kiosk exists, but full phone-lookup → 3-form → hash workflow incomplete. |
| Day-14 healed photo SMS prompt | ✅ EXISTS | Cron worker `deposit-deadline-reminders.ts` + SMS dispatch pattern established. Healed photo due_date auto-calculated. |
| Client portal (SMS magic link) | ❌ MISSING | No dedicated portal page. Consent forms have magic links, but no project/deposit/photo view. |
| Project completion automation | 🟡 PARTIAL | 30-day final-healed prompt missing. Photo release confirmation RPC exists. Google review prompt not found. Loyalty points credit via marketing module. 3-month referral + 6-month win-back in marketing flows. Birthday card flow wired. |
| Multi-tenancy (studio_id boundary) | ✅ EXISTS | RLS everywhere. studio_id is workspace partition. 72 migrations enforce tenant isolation. |

---

### FEATURE GATE AUDIT (23 keys defined)

**KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS in `lib/billing/feature-gate.ts`:**
- Always-on (all tiers): `booking` · `calendar` · `public_booking_page` · `digital_consent` · `client_crm` · `dodo_payments` · `custom_domain`
- Studio+ (`min: 'studio'`): `inventory` · `commissions` · `sms_reminders` · `marketing_basic` · `marketing_advanced` · `calendar_sync` · `referral_program` · `omnichannel_inbox` · `flash_events`
- Pro+ (`min: 'pro'`): `payroll` · `ai_design` · `ai_design_assistant` · `guest_artists` · `eu_reach` · `multi_location` · `analytics` · `messaging_ai_replies` · `projects`
- Enterprise (`min: 'enterprise'`): `white_label` · `api_access`

**Gap:** `messaging_ai_replies` gate defined but AI drafts for inbox not implemented.

---

### DEMO DATA COVERAGE

Demo seed at `scripts/seed/demo/modules/` covers: AI, audit, bookings, catalog (ink), clients, consent, flash-inventory, flash, inventory, marketing, members, messaging, payments, payroll, studio.

**Missing seed:** Client portal content, pre-session briefing data, project photo timeline refs, 1099 forms.

---

### SPRINT 12 DELIVERABLES (All Complete)

✅ Reporting (6 tabs: revenue, artists, clients, bookings, inventory, AI usage)
✅ Admin panel (studio search, impersonate, billing, audit log, feature flags)
✅ EU REACH ink passports + compliance export
✅ Robots.txt, sitemap.ts, error boundaries
✅ 72 migrations, 140+ routes, 644 TS/TSX files, 46 tests

---

### RECOMMENDATIONS FOR 50-100 SPRINT PLAN

**Tier 1 — High Risk (blocks launch readiness):**
1. **AI Assist Drafts** — Implement 3-job pipeline (inbound reply drafts, session summary, aftercare generation). Currently just design support. Needs Claude API integration + "never sends autonomously" safeguard.
2. **Allergies Persistent Banner** — Wire red banner to client detail layout, visible across all 8 tabs. Implement clear/edit audit logging.
3. **Client Portal via Magic Link** — Project page (deposit pool + photo timeline + next appointment + aftercare + read-only consent) accessible via SMS link.
4. **Pre-Session Briefing Push** — BullMQ worker collating allergies + pinned notes + last 3 sessions + deposit pool + outstanding forms, pushed 30 min before booking.

**Tier 2 — Feature Completeness (improves compliance to 95%):**
5. **Kiosk Pre-Session Intake** — Full phone-lookup → 3-form flow → single signature → hash + timestamp audit.
6. **Project Completion Automation** — 30-day final-healed prompt, photo release confirmation, Google review request (day 7), loyalty points credit, 3-month referral, 6-month win-back.
7. **1099-NEC Export** — Tax sub-ledger already exists; add RPC + CSV export for contractor earnings.
8. **Dispute Defense Pack Auto-Bundling** — Refund flow table + attached refund defense docs.
9. **Portfolio.inkos.studio Subdomain** — Custom domain routing for per-artist public pages.

**Tier 3 — Polish & Integrations:**
10. **Mailchimp Segment Export** — One-way sync from Analytics segments to Mailchimp campaigns.
11. **Channel-Tagged Inbox UI** — Message list shows channel origin badges (IG, WhatsApp, SMS, etc.).
12. **Flash Deposit-Gated Claim** — Flash pieces bookable with deposit hold confirmation.

---

### FILE PATHS FOR NAVIGATION

- **Feature gates:** `/lib/billing/feature-gate.ts` (23 keys, all listed)
- **Migrations:** `/supabase/migrations/` (72 files, see list from `find ... | tail -20`)

- **Demo data:** `scripts/seed/demo/modules/` (15 feature modules seeded)
- **Inbox integration:** `/app/api/webhooks/{instagram,whatsapp,twilio,resend-inbound,webchat}/route.ts`
- **Allergies column:** `/supabase/migrations/20260415*.sql` (clients table, column exists but UI banner not wired)
- **Deposit pool schema:** `projects.deposit_pool_cents` + `project_deposit_transactions` table (migration 20260422100200)
- **Photo timeline slots:** `/supabase/migrations/20260430100000_projects_v1_photos_and_refs.sql` (slot_type: before_skin | reference | s{N}_fresh | s{N}_healed)

---

**End Audit.** The build is **launch-ready** but **16 PDF features are missing or partial**, creating risk vectors for post-launch credibility. AI Assist (3 jobs), client portal, pre-session briefing, and allergies banner are the top 4 gaps to address in the next planning cycle.

content.text:
Audit done. User added tax point. Big architecture fork now — two payment layers, not one. Need lock decisions before sprint plan.

**Tax + payments — two distinct layers:**

| Layer | Who pays who | Tax challenge | Best tool |
|-------|-------------|---------------|-----------|
| **L1: SaaS billing** | Studio pays InkOS ($29/$59/$99/$199 per mo) | Global VAT/sales tax across US/EU/UK/AU | MoR provider (Dodo, Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) |
| **L2: In-studio billing** | Client (Karisa) pays studio (Sable & Sparrow), then commission split to artist (Miles) | Per-state US sales tax, marketplace split, 1099-NEC, dispute defense | Marketplace processor (Stripe Connect, Adyen for Platforms) |

Dodo+Paddle solve L1 well. **Neither does L2 marketplace splits.** PDF whole money model (deposit pool + 70/30 commission + tip routing + Stripe Connect destination charges) lives in L2.

Reality check on options:
- **Dodo only** = great L1 tax, custom L2 (manual splits, manual 1099, no dispute pack auto-bundle, no per-state tax line-by-line). Big build burden.
- **Paddle only** = great L1 tax, no L2 at all. Same burden.
- **Dodo (L1) + Stripe Connect (L2)** = best fit PDF spec. Two SDKs, two webhooks, two reconciliation paths.
- **Paddle (L1) + Stripe Connect (L2)** = same shape, swap MoR.
- **Stripe (L1+L2) with Stripe Tax** = single stack, Stripe Tax covers most US states + EU VAT + UK + AU. Not full MoR but close. Violates current CLAUDE.md Dodo lock.

Loading AskUserQuestion to lock decisions.

options.description: Keep Dodo as MoR for SaaS subscriptions (handles US sales tax + EU VAT + UK + AU on $29-$199 plans). Add Stripe Connect for in-studio marketplace: deposit pool charges, 70/30 commission destination charges, 1099-NEC, dispute defense pack, per-state tattoo-service tax line items. input.prompt:
Design a 60-90 sprint roadmap to take InkOS from current state (Sprint 12 complete, launch-ready) to full PDF spec compliance. Output is for a plan file, not implementation.

**Current state (audit findings):**
- 16 modules in PDF, 9 fully exist, 5 partial, 2 missing (AI Assist drafts/summary/aftercare; client portal magic link)
- Sprint 12 complete per CLAUDE.md
- 72 migrations, 511 routes, 286 components, 46 tests
- Dodo Payments wired (L1 SaaS billing only)
- Multi-channel inbox webhooks live but channel-tagged UI + AI drafts missing
- 7 of 8 client tabs exist, Financial tab + persistent allergies banner missing
- Photo timeline schema partial (slot_type column added 2026-04-30, but no sessions table — projects infer from bookings)
- /reports exists, named differently than PDF /analytics
- Demo seed exists but generic personas, NOT Maya/Miles/Karisa archetypes from PDF

**Locked decisions:**
- L1 SaaS billing: Dodo Payments (current, MoR for global SaaS tax)
- L2 in-studio billing: Stripe Connect (NEW — destination charges, 70/30 splits, Stripe Tax line items, dispute defense pack auto-bundling, 1099-NEC export)
- Public portfolio: portfolio.inkos.studio/[studio]/[artist] subdomain via wildcard DNS + middleware host rewrite
- 5 InkOS-specific agents: inkos-payments-lead, inkos-inbox-lead, inkos-canvas-lead, inkos-compliance-lead, inkos-brand-guardian

**Critical missing/partial features (from audit):**

Tier 1 — Launch blockers:
1. AI Assist 3 jobs (inbound reply drafts in studio voice, consult-to-3-bullet summary, aftercare auto-gen from session data) with "never sends autonomously" guard
2. Persistent red allergies banner across all 8 client tabs + audit-logged clear/edit
3. Client portal via SMS magic link (project view, deposit pool, photo timeline, next appt, aftercare, consent read-only)
4. 30-min pre-session briefing push (BullMQ worker, allergies + pinned notes + last 3 sessions + deposit pool + outstanding forms)
5. Financial tab on client detail page (8th tab)
6. Stripe Connect L2 marketplace (full payment overhaul — destination charges, deposit pool draw + new charge atomic, commission splits per Stripe Tax line, tip routing, refund proportional reversal)
7. Stripe Tax integration (per-state US tattoo-service tax — NYC 4.5% local, NJ 6.625%, CA/TX/FL/PA exempt for services, Iowa/MA tax permanent makeup, retail line vs service line)
8. 1099-NEC year-end export per artist
9. Dispute defense pack auto-bundling (signed consent + photo release + every session photo + chat history + deposit policy + receipt → one-click Stripe submit)

Tier 2 — Feature completeness:
10. Full kiosk pre-session intake (phone-lookup → 3 forms → single-finger signature → hash + timestamp)
11. Project completion automation (30-day final-healed prompt, photo release confirmation, day-7 review prompt, loyalty credit, 3-month referral, 6-month win-back, birthday card)
12. portfolio.inkos.studio subdomain with wildcard DNS + Enterprise custom domain CNAME
13. Channel-tagged inbox UI (IG/WhatsApp/SMS/Email badges per message)
14. Send Message channel-mismatch warning modal
15. Flash deposit-gated claim (bookable flash with deposit hold)
16. Flash Events full landing pages with public booking widget
17. AI Assist voice-learning (per-artist + per-studio tone learned from prior conversations)
18. Inventory REACH-EU compliance fail-fast at session-start (block session if non-compliant ink for EU client)
19. Tax sub-ledger quarterly export per location
20. Mailchimp segment sync (one-way push from Analytics segments)

Tier 3 — Polish, scale, production hardening:
21. Multi-location consolidated reporting (Enterprise tier)
22. White-label theming (Enterprise tier)
23. Public API + API access (Enterprise tier)
24. SSO for Enterprise
25. Multi-currency (UK GBP, EU EUR, AU AUD with Stripe Connect cross-border)
26. Guest artist invite + 80/20 split + travel/lodging carve-out + auto-deactivate on end date
27. Apprentice workflow (supervised consent, restricted Stripe access, 50/50 ramp split)
28. Studio onboarding wizard (Stripe Connect onboarding, BBP cert upload, state license verification, tax registration)
29. Performance hardening (Lighthouse LCP <2.5s, CLS <0.1 across all 16 modules)
30. Security hardening (re-audit RLS, audit log full coverage, GDPR/CCPA right-to-delete RPC battle-tested)
31. Mobile-first audit (Karisa journey is 100% phone — every flow phone-first)
32. Demo data: Maya/Miles/Karisa personas seeded (replace generic Inkhaus demo with PDF spec personas + 5-session koi sleeve project, allergies banner triggered, deposit pool with mid-project top-up, photo timeline filled)
33. Brand polish: every screen audited against 4 brand rules (editorial polish, rust earned, onyx CTAs, serif moments)
34. NOW sweep bar motion on dashboard timeline (only allowed dashboard motion)
35. Performance: tabular-nums on every number, semantic tokens only, no hex literals in components
36. AI cost monitoring + per-studio cost cap + Pro tier AI quota
37. Internationalization: en-US, en-GB, en-AU, fr, de (per Stripe Connect cross-border markets)
38. Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA across all 16 modules
39. PDF generation: receipts, 1099-NEC, REACH compliance certificates, dispute defense packages
40. Backup/DR: per-studio export (full data dump for studio leaving), automated daily snapshots, point-in-time restore tested

**Required output structure:**

A) **Epic groupings** — group sprints into 8-12 epics. Suggest names like "EPIC 1: Stripe Connect Marketplace (Sprints 13-22)". Each epic gets a 2-line goal + which Tier features it covers.

B) **Sprint-by-sprint table** — for each sprint:
   - Sprint number (continue from 13)
   - Sprint name (3-5 words)
   - Epic
   - Scope (3-5 bullets, concrete deliverables)
   - Dependencies (which sprints must ship first)
   - Lead agent (one of the 5 InkOS leads or a global agent)
   - Estimated complexity (S/M/L/XL based on lessons file: S=1 day, M=2-3 days, L=4-7 days, XL=needs splitting)
   - Risk flags (HIGH/MED/LOW with one-line reason)

C) **Sequencing logic** — explain why epics are ordered the way they are. What blocks what. What can run in parallel.

D) **Refactor sprints baked in** — every 5-7 feature sprints, insert a refactor sprint:
   - Type checker zero-warnings audit
   - Lighthouse performance audit
   - Sage full-codebase review
   - Lesson extraction (run /train)
   - Migration squash check
   These are non-negotiable — production grade requires this cadence.

E) **Quality gates per sprint** — every sprint ends with:
   - pnpm typecheck (zero errors)
   - pnpm build (no warnings)
   - Sage diff audit (zero CRITICAL findings)
   - Luna test pass (new tests for new code)
   - Demo seed regenerated and verified
   - inkos-lessons.md updated if new lesson surfaced

F) **Total sprint count** — give exact number based on the work, not arbitrary 50/100. Likely 60-90.

G) **Critical path** — the sequence of must-ship-first sprints to unlock launch (the Tier 1 list essentially). Estimate calendar weeks at the InkOS factory velocity demonstrated (13 sprints in 2 days per memory — but for production refactor cadence assume 1 sprint = 1-2 days realistic).

H) **Risk register** — top 10 risks with mitigation per risk:
   - Dodo + Stripe dual webhook reconciliation
   - Stripe Connect onboarding friction for non-US studios
   - REACH compliance regulatory drift
   - 1099-NEC vs W-2 misclassification per state
   - Photo timeline storage cost at scale
   - AI Assist hallucination liability
   - Allergy banner false-clear (audit gap)
   - Subdomain DNS ops at scale
   - Migrating existing demo studios to new payment stack
   - Cross-stack feature gate drift (23 keys + new ones)

Be exhaustive. The user wants 50-100 sprints organized so nothing falls through cracks. Better 80 well-organized sprints than 60 ambiguous ones. Output as structured markdown sections, ready for me to drop into a plan file. Target ~3000 words.

DO NOT WRITE CODE. This is roadmap planning only.

Design the architecture evolution + 5 project-specific agents for InkOS expansion. Output for a plan file, not implementation.

**Context:**
InkOS is a multi-tenant SaaS for tattoo studios (Stack A: Next.js 16 + Supabase + Railway + Tailwind 4 + shadcn). Currently Sprint 12 complete. PDF (`InkOS_In_Practice.pdf`) defines target product as 16 modules in 5 clusters. Need 60-90 sprint expansion.

**Architectural decisions locked:**
1. **L1 SaaS billing** = Dodo Payments (already wired, MoR for global tax on $29-$199 plans)
2. **L2 in-studio billing** = Stripe Connect (NEW — destination charges, deposit pool, 70/30 commission splits, Stripe Tax for US per-state tattoo-service tax, dispute defense pack, 1099-NEC export)
3. **Public portfolio domain** = portfolio.inkos.studio/[studio]/[artist] (subdomain, wildcard DNS, middleware host rewrite)
4. **5 project-specific agents** at `.claude/agents/` inside InkOS repo

**Current schema highlights (from audit):**
- 72 migrations, RLS everywhere, studio_id is tenant boundary
- `projects` table with `deposit_pool_cents` columns (in/applied/available/refundable)
- `project_deposit_transactions` child table
- `project_progress_photos` with slot_type enum (before_skin, reference, s{N}_fresh, s{N}_healed)
- `clients.allergies` column exists but UI banner not wired
- `bookings` table — no separate `sessions` table (sessions inferred from bookings)
- `conversations` + `messages` for omnichannel inbox (IG/WhatsApp/SMS/Email/Webchat all wired)
- 23 feature gate keys in `lib/billing/feature-gate.ts`
- BullMQ + Redis for background jobs (AI designs, SMS, email, PDF gen)
- Pino structured logging
- Dodo Payments via lazy-init client at `lib/dodo/`

**Forbidden per CLAUDE.md (cannot deviate):**
- Vercel (Railway only)
- Pages Router (App Router only)
- Prisma / any ORM (Supabase client + generated types only)
- npm/yarn (pnpm only)
- Hand-edited types.ts (always `pnpm db:types`)
- `any` TypeScript
- Hex literals in components (Bone/Onyx/Stone/Rust tokens only)
- Default Tailwind shadows (use shadow-soft/card/lift)
- Hardcoded plan-tier checks (use hasFeature/<FeatureGate>)

**Required output structure (~2500 words):**

## PART A — DUAL-STACK PAYMENT ARCHITECTURE

### A.1 — L1 (SaaS) Dodo flow (current, just document)
What stays the same. Webhook handler, subscription lifecycle, plan upgrades, dunning.

### A.2 — L2 (in-studio) Stripe Connect flow (NEW)
- **Onboarding flow** for studios: Stripe Connect Express account creation, KYC, tax docs (W-9 for US, equivalent for international), connected_account_id stored on `studios` table
- **Onboarding flow for artists**: each artist gets their own connected sub-account (or single connected per studio with manual splits — recommend which and why)
- **Charge flow** for client payments: PaymentIntent with destination charge, transfer_data[destination] = artist's connected account, application_fee_amount = studio's commission. Document the exact Stripe call shape.
- **Deposit pool charge flow**: holding charges in studio's main connected account (separate balance), drawing from pool at session settlement, atomic with new charge
- **Tip routing**: separate transfer to artist's connected account post-capture
- **Tax line items**: Stripe Tax `automatic_tax: true` for US sales tax, manual tax_rates fallback for jurisdictions Stripe doesn't cover
- **Refund flow**: reverse the original charge, automatically reverse the application_fee + transfer (Stripe Connect refund mechanics)
- **Dispute flow**: webhook on charge.dispute.created → auto-bundle defense package, attach to dispute via Stripe API
- **1099-NEC export**: query `transfers` API per artist per year, export CSV with TIN/SSN/EIN, generate IRS form

### A.3 — Database schema additions
List new tables/columns needed:
- `stripe_connected_accounts` (account_id, type [studio | artist], onboarding_status, capabilities, country, default_currency, restricted_reason)
- `stripe_charges` (intent_id, charge_id, transfer_id, application_fee_id, status, currency_amount, tax_amount, fee_amount)
- `stripe_disputes` (dispute_id, charge_id, evidence_due_by, defense_pack_url, submission_status)
- `tax_remittance_ledger` (location_id, jurisdiction, period, amount_collected, amount_remitted, remittance_date)
- `commission_splits` (booking_id, artist_id, base_amount, commission_pct, tip_amount, applied_from_pool, stripe_transfer_id)
- `dispute_defense_packs` (dispute_id, signed_consent_url, photo_release_url, session_photos_urls[], chat_history_url, deposit_policy_text, receipt_url, bundle_pdf_url)
- `nec_1099_exports` (year, artist_id, total_paid, federal_id, state_id, csv_url, generated_at)
Plus `bookings` table evolution: add `stripe_charge_id`, `stripe_transfer_id`, `commission_split_id`, `tax_amount_cents`.

### A.4 — Webhook reconciliation
Two webhook sources (Dodo for SaaS + Stripe for L2). Both need idempotency keys, replay protection, audit log of every event. Document the reconciliation pattern — single `webhook_events` table partitioned by source, replay queue per source, hourly cron compares Dodo subscriptions vs InkOS state and Stripe charges vs InkOS state.

### A.5 — Failure modes + handling
- Stripe Connect account in `restricted_soon` → studio sees banner, must update KYC
- Cross-border charge with FX → record original + settled amounts
- Dispute lost → reverse commission, debit artist's next payout (or claw back from connected account if balance positive)
- Refund issued but transfer already paid out → use `reverse_transfer: true`
- Tax remittance failure → don't block charge, queue for manual review

## PART B — DATA MODEL EVOLUTION

For each module gap from PDF, list new tables/columns needed:

### B.1 — Sessions as first-class entity
PDF treats Session as distinct from Booking (a booking is one calendar slot, but a project has 5 sessions and each session might span multiple bookings if it goes long). Currently codebase infers sessions from bookings. Recommend: add `sessions` table with `project_id`, `session_number`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `actual_hours`, `bookings_ids[]` (array of bookings rolled into this session), `pre_session_briefing_sent_at`, `pre_session_briefing_payload`. Keep bookings as the calendar primitive; sessions as the project-level event.

### B.2 — Persistent allergies banner
Add `client_medical_flags` table: `client_id`, `flag_type` (allergy | medication | condition | sensitivity), `severity` (informational | warning | critical), `description`, `cleared_at`, `cleared_by`, `cleared_reason`. Existing `clients.allergies` migrates to this table. Banner reads `WHERE cleared_at IS NULL AND severity IN ('warning','critical')`. Every clear is audit-logged.

### B.3 — Client portal magic link
Add `client_portal_sessions` table: `token`, `client_id`, `expires_at`, `used_at`, `scopes[]`. Token is signed JWT with short expiry (15 min from SMS click), refreshed on use. Public route `/portal/[token]` validates and renders read-only project view.

### B.4 — Pre-session briefing
Add `pre_session_briefings` table: `session_id`, `payload` (JSON snapshot of allergies + pinned notes + last 3 sessions + deposit pool + outstanding forms), `pushed_at`, `read_at`, `delivered_via` (push | sms | email).
BullMQ cron: 30 min before each session, build payload, push to artist via mobile app push notification + SMS fallback.

### B.5 — Photo timeline completeness
Add `session_photos` table linking `sessions` ↔ `project_progress_photos`. Allows multiple fresh photos per session (mid-session, end-of-session). Healed photo at Day 14 is single per session.

### B.6 — AI Assist
Add `ai_drafts` table: `conversation_id`, `draft_text`, `model`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `cost_cents`, `accepted_at`, `accepted_by`, `edited_text`. Audit: every draft is logged, accepted or not, edited text vs original recorded for voice-learning.
Add `ai_voice_profiles` table: per-studio + per-artist tone fingerprint, computed nightly from last 30 days of sent messages.

### B.7 — Loyalty + referrals
Add `loyalty_ledger`, `loyalty_tiers`, `referral_codes`, `referral_redemptions`. Document fields.

### B.8 — Marketing flows
Add `marketing_flow_runs` table tracking each flow execution per client (win-back, birthday, review, referral, win-back-2). Idempotent — never re-fire on same trigger.

## PART C — 5 INKOS-SPECIFIC AGENTS

For each agent, give:
- **Agent name** (file: `.claude/agents/[name].md`)
- **Role** (1-line)
- **Domain ownership** (3-5 areas, mutually exclusive)
- **Loads at start** (which knowledge files: PDF + CLAUDE.md + lessons + relevant memory patterns)
- **Tools** (Read/Write/Edit/Bash/etc)
- **Reports to** (Yash for executive, Arya/Atlas for tech, etc — match factory roster)
- **Boundaries** (what they DON'T do, to prevent overlap)
- **Quality gates** (what they must verify before handoff)
- **Escalation rules** (when to escalate to global agents)

The 5 agents:

### C.1 — inkos-payments-lead
Owns: Dodo SaaS billing (L1) + Stripe Connect marketplace (L2) + Stripe Tax + tax remittance per-jurisdiction + 1099-NEC + dispute defense + commission splits + deposit pool atomic operations + payout schedules + chargeback recovery.

### C.2 — inkos-inbox-lead
Owns: multi-channel webhook reconciliation (IG + WhatsApp + Twilio SMS + Resend email + webchat) + AI Assist 3 jobs (drafts in voice, summary, aftercare) + voice profile training + channel-mismatch warnings + auto-reply rules + Send Message modal + conversation lifecycle.

### C.3 — inkos-canvas-lead
Owns: calendar (multi-artist columns + drag-resched + auto-blocks + deposit-gate) + bookings + sessions (NEW first-class entity) + 30-min pre-session briefing push + iPad kiosk pre-session intake + photo timeline (refs/stencil/fresh/healed) + Day-14 healed-photo SMS prompt.

### C.4 — inkos-compliance-lead
Owns: REACH ink registry (EU compliance) + MoCRA (US ink compliance) + BBP cert tracking + state license tracking + age-of-consent per state + 1099 vs W-2 ABC test classification + GDPR/CCPA data deletion + photo release granular toggles + minor consent w/ guardian + audit log integrity + dispute defense pack docs.

### C.5 — inkos-brand-guardian
Owns: 4-color palette enforcement (Bone/Onyx/Stone/Rust only — reject any PR with hex outside) + 2-font discipline (Inter for workhorse, Instrument Serif italic for moments only) + voice rules (editorial, no exclamations, no "Amazing!") + spacing/shadow tokens (no Tailwind defaults) + tabular-nums on every number + 4 brand rules from CLAUDE.md + email templates + receipt PDFs + portfolio public pages + landing page copy.

## PART D — CLAUDE.md UPDATES

List the exact additions/changes needed to `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS/CLAUDE.md` to reflect:
1. Dual-stack payments (Dodo L1 + Stripe Connect L2)
2. Sessions as first-class entity
3. The 5 InkOS agents and their dispatch rules
4. portfolio.inkos.studio subdomain wildcard DNS
5. PDF as authoritative reference (load it on every payments/projects/calendar/forms touch)
6. New forbidden list additions (no manual commission splits outside Stripe Connect, no in-app payouts to artists, no untested webhook handlers, etc)
7. Updated tier feature matrix (sync with PDF tier definitions)
8. New TIPS sections referencing inkos-lessons.md and PDF chapters

## PART E — KNOWLEDGE GRAPH FOR AGENTS

What knowledge file each of the 5 agents should auto-load on every dispatch (full file paths). Layer it: Tier 1 (always loaded) + Tier 2 (loaded for specific task types) + Tier 3 (loaded only if explicitly needed).

Keep it production-grade. The user wants nothing missed. Better 2500 deep words than 1500 vague ones.

DO NOT WRITE CODE. Architecture + agent design only. Output as structured markdown sections.

# InkOS Sprint 13–87 Roadmap: Launch-Ready → Full PDF Spec Compliance

**Total sprints: 75** (Sprints 13–87), grouped into **11 epics**, with **11 baked-in refactor sprints** at every 5–7 feature sprints. Critical-path-to-launch (Tier 1 only): **Sprints 13–34** (~3–6 weeks at 1–2 days/sprint).

> **Audit reconciliation:** the audit lists Financial tab as missing but `app/(app)/clients/[id]/financial/page.tsx` exists on disk. Treating this as "scaffold present, content/data integration missing" — collapsed into the allergies banner sprint rather than its own sprint.

---

## A) Epic Groupings

### EPIC 1 — Stripe Connect Marketplace Foundation (Sprints 13–22)
**Goal:** Replace single-rail Dodo billing with dual-rail (Dodo SaaS L1 + Stripe Connect L2) and ship the entire in-studio money pipeline: destination charges, deposit pool atomicity, commission splits, refunds, tip routing.
**Tier coverage:** T1 #6, #7, #8, #9.

### EPIC 2 — AI Assist & Inbox Channel Layer (Sprints 24–30)
**Goal:** Ship the three never-autonomous AI Assist jobs, channel-tagged inbox UI with mismatch warnings, voice-learning per artist/studio, and AI cost monitoring.
**Tier coverage:** T1 #1, T2 #13, #14, #17, T3 #36.

### EPIC 3 — Client Safety & Portal (Sprints 31–37)
**Goal:** Persistent allergies banner across all 8 client tabs with audit-logged clears, SMS magic-link client portal, 30-min pre-session briefing push, Financial tab data integration.
**Tier coverage:** T1 #2, #3, #4, #5.

### EPIC 4 — Sessions, Projects & Photo Timeline (Sprints 39–45)
**Goal:** Promote sessions to a first-class table, complete photo timeline (slot_type semantics, healed-photo prompts, release confirmation), project completion automation (30-day, day-7, 3-month, 6-month, birthday).
**Tier coverage:** T2 #11, T3 #39 (PDF generation pieces).

### EPIC 5 — Public Surface & Portfolio Subdomain (Sprints 46–51)
**Goal:** Ship `portfolio.inkos.studio/[studio]/[artist]` via wildcard DNS + proxy.ts host rewrite, Enterprise custom domain CNAME, full kiosk pre-session intake, flash deposit-gated claim, flash event landing pages.
**Tier coverage:** T2 #10, #12, #15, #16.

### EPIC 6 — Compliance, Tax & Reporting Refactor (Sprints 53–59)
**Goal:** REACH-EU fail-fast at session start, tax sub-ledger quarterly export, /reports → /analytics rename + segment-driven Mailchimp sync, multi-location consolidated reporting (Enterprise).
**Tier coverage:** T2 #18, #19, #20, T3 #21.

### EPIC 7 — Enterprise Tier & White-Label (Sprints 60–65)
**Goal:** White-label theming, public API + scoped tokens, SSO (SAML/OIDC), Enterprise feature flags wired through 23-key registry.
**Tier coverage:** T3 #22, #23, #24.

### EPIC 8 — International & Multi-Currency (Sprints 67–71)
**Goal:** Multi-currency (GBP/EUR/AUD) via Stripe Connect cross-border, i18n (en-US/en-GB/en-AU/fr/de), region-aware tax, currency-correct ledger.
**Tier coverage:** T3 #25, #37.

### EPIC 9 — Workforce & Onboarding Polish (Sprints 72–76)
**Goal:** Guest artist invite + 80/20 + travel/lodging carve-out + auto-deactivate, apprentice supervised workflow + 50/50 ramp, studio onboarding wizard (Connect + BBP + state license + tax registration).
**Tier coverage:** T3 #26, #27, #28.

### EPIC 10 — Performance, Security, Mobile, A11y Hardening (Sprints 78–83)
**Goal:** Lighthouse LCP <2.5s / CLS <0.1 across all 16 modules, RLS re-audit, audit log full coverage, GDPR/CCPA right-to-delete RPC battle-tested, mobile-first re-audit on Karisa journey, WCAG 2.1 AA.
**Tier coverage:** T3 #29, #30, #31, #38.

### EPIC 11 — Brand, Demo, PDF & DR Final Pass (Sprints 84–87)
**Goal:** Maya/Miles/Karisa demo personas + 5-session koi sleeve, brand polish across every screen against 4 brand rules, PDF generation (receipts/1099-NEC/REACH/dispute packs), backup-DR per-studio export + PITR.
**Tier coverage:** T3 #32, #33, #34, #35, #39, #40.

---

## B) Sprint-by-Sprint Table

Format per row: **#**, name, epic, scope, deps, lead agent, complexity, risk.

**Notation:** Lead agents — `payments-lead` = inkos-payments-lead, `inbox-lead` = inkos-inbox-lead, `canvas-lead` = inkos-canvas-lead, `compliance-lead` = inkos-compliance-lead, `brand-guardian` = inkos-brand-guardian. Globals: Dato, Koda, Vega, Pixel, Quill, Luna, Sage, Bolt, Vex, Hawk.

### EPIC 1 — Stripe Connect Marketplace (S13–S22)

## C) Sequencing Logic

**Why epics are ordered this way:**

1. **Epic 1 (Stripe Connect) ships first** because every later money-touching feature (deposit pool in portal S34, flash deposit-gate S49, lifecycle credits S43, multi-currency S67, apprentice splits S73, dispute packs S86) depends on the new payment rail. Building any of those before Connect lands means rework.
2. **Epic 2 (AI Assist) before Epic 3 (Client Safety)** because the inbound-reply-draft job lives in inbox UI that Epic 2 also rebuilds — building portal first would force a second pass on inbox.
3. **Epic 3 (Allergies + Portal + Briefing + Financial)** is the launch-blocker tier completion — these four sprints close the Tier 1 list. Critical path ends at S37.
4. **Epic 4 (Sessions table promotion)** runs after launch-critical because it's a data-shape migration; doing it earlier risks losing Tier 1 velocity.
5. **Epic 5 (Public surface)** depends on portal foundation (S33) and brand pass (S38), and unblocks Enterprise custom domain (S47 → S60+).
6. **Epic 6 (Compliance/Tax/Analytics)** depends on payments + sessions; tax sub-ledger needs Connect, REACH fail-fast needs sessions table.
7. **Epic 7 (Enterprise)** depends on multi-location data shapes from Epic 6 (#57).
8. **Epic 8 (i18n + multi-currency)** is intentionally after Enterprise because cross-border Connect needs Connect at maturity.
9. **Epic 9 (Workforce + Onboarding)** depends on every prior epic — onboarding wizard touches Connect, brand, license, BBP, tax.
10. **Epic 10 (Hardening)** is the penultimate epic by design — you can't harden until features are complete; doing it earlier means re-hardening every sprint.
11. **Epic 11 (Brand/Demo/PDF/DR)** is the final polish layer. Demo personas must reflect the *finished* product, not a moving target.

**What can run in parallel:**
- S13 (schema) ‖ S14 (webhook wiring) once Dato finalizes RPC signatures.
- S19 (Stripe Tax) ‖ S14–S18 since tax matrix is independent of charge flow.
- S26 (consult summary) ‖ S25 (reply drafts) — independent AI jobs.
- S39 (sessions table) ‖ S40 (photo slots) only if Dato writes both migrations cleanly.
- S46 (subdomain) ‖ S48 (kiosk) — different surfaces.
- S60 (white-label) ‖ S61–S63 (API) — can fan out.
- S68 (i18n) ‖ S69 (fr/de copy) once locale shells exist.

**What blocks what (hard dependency edges):**
- S13 → everything in Epic 1.
- S22 (refactor gate) → Epic 2 start.
- S37 → Epic 4 start (sessions migration on stable foundation).
- S39 → S40 → S41 → S42 → S43 → S44 (lifecycle is sequential).
- S65 (feature-key wiring) → Epic 7 launchable.

## D) Refactor Sprints — Baked In, Non-Negotiable

Refactor sprints fire **every 5–7 feature sprints**. Each refactor sprint:

- **Type checker zero-warnings audit** — `pnpm typecheck` zero errors AND zero warnings; `lib/supabase/types.ts` regenerated with `pnpm db:types`.
- **Lighthouse performance audit** — every changed route checked; LCP <2.5s, CLS <0.1, INP <200ms; regressions blocked.
- **Sage full-codebase review** — diff-mode against last refactor checkpoint; CRITICAL findings blocking; HIGH findings tracked.
- **Lesson extraction** — `/train` runs against the last 5–7 sprints; updates `~/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md`.
- **Migration squash check** — ensure no orphan migrations, no skipped numbers, all RPCs have shared TS interfaces, types regenerated.

**Refactor sprint locations:** S22, S31, S37, S45, S52, S59, S66, S71, S77, S83. (10 refactor sprints embedded; Epic 11 ends with S87 final-DR which functions as the pre-launch hardening checkpoint.)

## E) Quality Gates — Every Sprint Ends With

These run in the same order, every single sprint, no exceptions:

1. **`pnpm typecheck`** — zero errors.
2. **`pnpm build`** — zero warnings.
3. **Sage diff audit** — zero CRITICAL findings; HIGH findings logged with explicit defer rationale.
4. **Luna test pass** — new tests for new code (unit + integration where applicable + Playwright for any new public flow).
5. **Demo seed regenerated and verified** — `pnpm db:seed:demo:reset && pnpm db:seed:demo:verify` exits 0; new feature visible on demo studio.
6. **`inkos-lessons.md` updated** — any new lesson surfaced (RPC mismatch, drift, gotcha) appended with sprint reference.

If any gate fails, the sprint is **not closed**. No "fix in next sprint" — fix in *this* sprint or extend the sprint.

## PART A — DUAL-STACK PAYMENT ARCHITECTURE

### A.1 — L1 (SaaS) Dodo flow — DOCUMENT, DO NOT TOUCH

Status: shipped Sprint 4, hardened through Sprint 12. Anything in this section is "read-only, audit-only, do not refactor without `inkos-payments-lead` sign-off."

- **Client:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS/lib/dodo/client.ts` — lazy-init Proxy singleton, never construct at module evaluation time (env vars not loaded yet at build).
- **Webhook:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS/app/api/webhooks/dodo/route.ts` — must follow `standardwebhooks` spec: `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature` headers verified by `timingSafeEqual` (constant-time HMAC), never `===`.
- **Subscription lifecycle handled events:** `subscription.active` / `subscription.cancelled` / `subscription.failed` / `subscription.renewed` / `payment.succeeded` / `payment.failed`. Each event writes to `subscriptions` table via service-role client (bypasses RLS). Web app code is read-only on this table — write-only-by-webhook is locked in CLAUDE.md §7.7.
- **Plan upgrade flow:** `lib/dodo/checkout.ts` builds a Dodo checkout session with `return_url` (NOT `success_url` — gotcha #2 in inkos-lessons §6), customer's `billing.country` is required (ISO-3166 two-letter, gotcha #5).
- **Customer portal:** `lib/dodo/portal.ts` returns `{ link }` from Dodo (NOT `{ url }`, gotcha #3) — embedded in `/settings/billing`.
- **Dunning:** Dodo handles retry schedule + dunning emails; we store `subscription_status` and surface Bone/Stone-tinted banner on `/dashboard` when status ∈ `past_due, paused, cancelled`.
- **Tax:** Dodo is Merchant of Record — they handle global VAT/GST/sales-tax. We never collect tax on the L1 transaction. Receipts come from Dodo, branded as Dodo.

**This stack does not change. The `inkos-payments-lead` agent owns guarding it from regression as Stripe Connect lands.**

### A.2 — L2 (in-studio) Stripe Connect flow — NEW

This is the marketplace layer: studios charge clients for tattoo services, InkOS routes funds with commission splits, tax collection, and 1099 reporting. Stripe Connect Express is the only viable model — full "Custom" KYC is too heavy for an artist who just wants to get paid.

**Recommendation: ONE connected account per studio (Express), commission splits handled in-app via `application_fee_amount`, artist payouts via separate `transfers` API call to per-artist Stripe Express accounts when the artist enables payouts.**

Rationale: simpler KYC for studios (one Express account onboarding), but artists who want direct payouts get their own sub-account so the studio doesn't hold their money beyond the daily cycle. This matches Vagaro/Mindbody mechanics and avoids the W-2 pseudo-employer trap (which a single-pool model would create per IRS ABC test — see compliance section).

**Onboarding flow — studio:**
1. Owner clicks "Enable in-studio payments" in `/settings/payments`.
2. Server creates Stripe Express account: `stripe.accounts.create({ type: 'express', country, capabilities: { card_payments, transfers, tax_reporting_us_1099_nec } })`.
3. Server stores `stripe_connected_accounts` row, returns `account_links.create()` URL → studio redirected to Stripe-hosted KYC.
4. Webhook `account.updated` flips `onboarding_status` from `pending` → `active` when `charges_enabled` and `payouts_enabled` are true.
5. Studio sees Bone/Onyx-tinted banner on `/dashboard` until KYC complete.

**Onboarding flow — artist:**
1. Artist opts in via `/settings/my-payouts`.
2. Server creates a second Express account using `account_links.create()` with the artist's email + TIN/SSN.
3. Webhook `account.updated` flips that artist row's `onboarding_status` to `active`.
4. Until artist completes KYC, their commission accrues to the studio's connected balance and the studio pays them via existing payroll/1099 path.

**Charge flow — exact Stripe call shape (destination charge model):**

```
stripe.paymentIntents.create({
  amount: total_cents,                    // base + tip + tax
  currency: 'usd',
  customer: client_stripe_customer_id,
  payment_method: pm_id,
  confirm: true,
  application_fee_amount: studio_commission_cents,  // 30% in 70/30 split
  transfer_data: { destination: artist_connected_account_id },
  on_behalf_of: artist_connected_account_id,
  automatic_tax: { enabled: true },       // Stripe Tax for US per-state
  metadata: {
    studio_id, artist_id, booking_id, project_id, session_id,
    deposit_pool_drawdown_cents,          // for atomic settlement
    inkos_idempotency_key                 // dedupe in webhook reconciliation
  }
})
```

If the artist hasn't onboarded their own account, `transfer_data.destination` = studio's account, and the studio reconciles internally (artist still gets their share via in-house payroll, no 1099 from Stripe direct).

**Deposit pool charge flow (atomic with new charge):**
- `projects.deposit_pool_cents_available` is the source of truth.
- At session settlement: a Postgres RPC `apply_deposit_to_session(project_id, session_id, draw_cents)` runs in a single transaction:
  1. Verify `available >= draw_cents`.
  2. Decrement `available`, increment `applied`, insert `project_deposit_transactions` row with `kind='applied'`.
  3. The PaymentIntent's `amount` is `(session_total - draw_cents)` — only the balance is charged through Stripe.
  4. If PaymentIntent fails, RPC rolls back (transaction wraps both DB write and external call indirectly via SAGA pattern: write deposit txn as `pending_apply` first, only flip to `applied` on `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook).
- Deposit-only charges (collected at booking creation) hit the studio's connected balance via a charge with NO `transfer_data` — they sit in studio float until applied.

**Tip routing:** Tips are captured in the same PaymentIntent as the session charge (line item `tip_amount_cents`). The `application_fee_amount` excludes the tip, so 100% of tip flows to the artist's `transfer_data.destination`. Studios that pool tips can override this in settings — the override flips the split to: tip goes to studio account, daily transfer cron splits per studio's pool rule.

**Tax line items:** `automatic_tax: { enabled: true }` enables Stripe Tax. Stripe maintains rates for all US states + most EU/CA/AU jurisdictions. For jurisdictions Stripe doesn't cover (e.g., a few rural EU regions, certain tribal-land tattoo taxes), fallback to `tax_rates: [tx_id]` populated manually per location in `/settings/tax`. Tax amount is recorded on the charge metadata AND in `tax_remittance_ledger` for monthly remittance.

**Refund flow:** `stripe.refunds.create({ payment_intent, amount, reverse_transfer: true, refund_application_fee: true })`. `reverse_transfer: true` claws the artist's share back from their connected balance (or debits next payout if balance is insufficient). `refund_application_fee: true` returns the studio's commission portion. We mirror by inserting a `commission_splits` row with `kind='reversal'` and re-incrementing `deposit_pool_cents_available` if the refund originated from pool drawdown.

**Dispute flow:** Webhook on `charge.dispute.created` →
1. Insert `stripe_disputes` row.
2. Enqueue BullMQ job `assemble-dispute-defense-pack`.
3. Job pulls: signed consent form PDF (Sprint 6), photo release PDF, all `project_progress_photos` for the session, conversation thread snapshot from `messages`, deposit policy text, original receipt → bundles into one PDF, uploads to private Storage, stores URL.
4. Submit evidence via `stripe.disputes.update(id, { evidence: { customer_signature, customer_communication, receipt, service_documentation, ... } })` 24h before `evidence_due_by`.
5. If lost: Stripe debits studio's balance; we mirror via a `commission_splits` reversal row clawing artist's share, OR if artist balance is negative, log to `payroll` for next-cycle deduction.

**1099-NEC export:** Annual cron at year-end queries `stripe.transfers.list` per artist's connected account, groups by tax year, exports CSV with `name, TIN/SSN/EIN, federal_id, state_id, total_paid, address` to `/admin/tax-exports`. For studios on the studio-pool model (artist has no own connected account), 1099-NEC is generated from `commission_splits` table directly. Stripe also offers `tax_reporting_us_1099_nec` capability — we enable it on every connected account so Stripe can issue the form too, and we cross-check.

### A.4 — Webhook reconciliation

Two webhook sources, one ledger:

- **`webhook_events`** — `id, source ENUM('dodo' | 'stripe'), event_id (UNIQUE on (source, event_id)), event_type, payload JSONB, signature_verified BOOL, processed_at, error TEXT, retry_count INT, created_at`.
- Idempotency: `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (source, event_id) DO NOTHING` is the first write of every webhook handler. If conflict, return 200 immediately.
- Replay protection: Dodo + Stripe both include timestamp headers; reject events older than 5 minutes.
- Audit: every event row keeps full payload for 90 days, then archived.
- **Reconciliation cron (hourly):**
  - For Dodo: list active subscriptions, compare against `subscriptions` table — flag drift.
  - For Stripe: list charges in last 25h, compare against `stripe_charges` — flag drift, log to `/admin/payments/reconciliation` for human review.
- Replay queue: `BullMQ` queue `webhook-replay` per source; failed events auto-retry 3× with exponential backoff (30s, 5m, 1h), then dead-letter for manual.

### A.5 — Failure modes + handling

| Mode | Detection | Handling |
|------|-----------|----------|
| Stripe account `restricted_soon` | `account.updated` webhook | Onyx banner on `/dashboard`, link to KYC. Charges still work. |
| Cross-border charge with FX | PaymentIntent metadata has `presentment_currency` ≠ `settlement_currency` | Record both `amount_cents` (settled) and `presentment_amount_cents` on `stripe_charges`. |
| Dispute lost | `charge.dispute.closed` event with `status='lost'` | Clawback via `commission_splits` reversal; if artist balance negative, log to `payroll` for deduction next cycle. |
| Refund after payout | Refund call returns `requires_action` for transfer reversal | Use `reverse_transfer: true` always; if artist balance positive, instant claw; if negative, debit next payout. |
| Tax remittance failure | Stripe Tax reporting API error | Don't block charge; queue `tax_remittance_ledger` row as `status='manual_review'` for `inkos-compliance-lead` review. |
| Restricted account, charge attempted | Stripe returns `account_invalid` | Bone/Onyx banner blocking checkout, redirect to `/settings/payments/onboarding`. |

## PART B — DATA MODEL EVOLUTION

### B.1 — Sessions as first-class entity

Currently sessions are inferred from `bookings` + `project_progress_photos` slot enums (`s1_fresh`, `s2_healed`, …). PDF treats Session as a project-level event distinct from Booking (a calendar slot).

**New table `sessions`:** `id, studio_id, project_id, session_number (INT), status (planned | in_progress | completed | cancelled | no_show), planned_at, started_at, completed_at, planned_hours, actual_hours, pre_session_briefing_payload JSONB, pre_session_briefing_pushed_at, pre_session_briefing_read_at, notes, created_at`.

**Bridge:** `session_bookings (session_id, booking_id)` — many-to-many because a single session can span two bookings if it runs long.

Existing `project_progress_photos.slot_type` enum migrates: `s{N}_fresh` rows get `session_id` populated. Bookings keep their existing fields; the `sessions` table is the project-level rollup.

### B.2 — Persistent allergies banner

`clients.allergies` column exists but has no UI banner. Migrate to:

**New table `client_medical_flags`:** `id, studio_id, client_id, flag_type ENUM(allergy | medication | condition | sensitivity), severity ENUM(informational | warning | critical), description, source ENUM(intake_form | artist_added | client_self), cleared_at, cleared_by, cleared_reason, created_at`.

Banner reads `WHERE cleared_at IS NULL AND severity IN ('warning','critical')`. Every clear is audit-logged via existing `lib/audit.ts`. Migration backfills existing `clients.allergies` text → flags rows with `severity='warning'` (manual triage upgrade to critical via UI).

### B.3 — Client portal magic link

**New table `client_portal_sessions`:** `id, token (UNIQUE), client_id, studio_id, scopes TEXT[], expires_at, used_at, created_at, ip_address (INET), user_agent`.

Token = signed JWT (HS256, secret in env), 15-min expiry. Public route `/portal/[token]` validates via `createPublicClient` (anon Supabase + RPC). RPC `client_portal_get_view(token)` returns project + photos + deposit pool + outstanding forms — all read-only.

### B.4 — Pre-session briefing

**New table `pre_session_briefings`:** `id, session_id (UNIQUE), studio_id, payload JSONB (allergies + pinned notes + last 3 sessions + deposit pool + outstanding forms), pushed_at, read_at, delivered_via ENUM(push | sms | email), retry_count`.

**BullMQ cron `pre-session-briefing-builder`** runs every 5 min: finds sessions with `planned_at` between now+25min and now+35min where briefing not yet built. Builds payload from: `client_medical_flags`, `pinned_items` (existing table), last 3 `sessions` rows for this client, current `projects.deposit_pool_cents_available`, any `consent_form_submissions` outstanding. Pushes via `lib/messaging/send.ts` (push notification via existing channel + SMS fallback if not opened in 10 min).

### B.5 — Photo timeline completeness

**New table `session_photos`:** `id, session_id, project_progress_photo_id, capture_phase ENUM(reference | stencil | mid_session | end_session | day_14_healed), captured_at`.

This allows multiple fresh photos per session (the slot-enum approach forced one). The Day-14 healed-photo SMS prompt is a BullMQ scheduled job: at `completed_at + 14 days`, send SMS with magic-link upload portal.

### B.6 — AI Assist

**New tables:**
- `ai_drafts` — `id, conversation_id, message_id (FK nullable, set when accepted), draft_text, model, prompt_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_cents, accepted_at, accepted_by, edited_text, created_at`.
- `ai_voice_profiles` — `id, studio_id, artist_id (nullable for studio-wide), tone_fingerprint JSONB (vocab, sentence length distribution, emoji rate, exclamation rate, formality score), example_message_ids UUID[], computed_at`.

Nightly cron at 03:00 studio-tz pulls last 30 days of sent `messages` per artist, computes fingerprint, stores. Drafts are generated by passing the fingerprint + last 5 conversation messages to Claude. Audit: every draft row records original + accepted/edited text — feeds future fine-tune corpora.

### B.7 — Loyalty + referrals

- `loyalty_ledger` — `id, studio_id, client_id, points_delta, reason (booking_completed | review_left | birthday_bonus | manual), reference_id, balance_after, created_at`.
- `loyalty_tiers` — `id, studio_id, name, min_points, perks JSONB`.
- `referral_codes` — `id, studio_id, code (UNIQUE), client_id (referrer), reward_kind (credit_cents | percent_off | free_consult), reward_value, expires_at, max_redemptions, redemptions_count`.
- `referral_redemptions` — `id, code_id, referred_client_id, booking_id, reward_applied_cents, created_at`.

### B.8 — Marketing flows

**New table `marketing_flow_runs`:** `id, studio_id, flow_kind ENUM(win_back | birthday | review | referral | win_back_2 | post_session_aftercare), client_id, trigger_at, fired_at, channel, message_id, idempotency_key (UNIQUE per (flow_kind, client_id, trigger_window))`.

Idempotency: never re-fire on same trigger window (e.g., birthday flow keyed by `(client_id, year)`).

> Plan target: 60-90 sprint expansion from current Sprint 12 (launch-ready, 72 migrations) to full 16-module / 5-cluster product per `InkOS_In_Practice.pdf`.

## PART A — DUAL-STACK PAYMENT ARCHITECTURE

### A.1 — L1 (SaaS) Dodo flow — DOCUMENT, DO NOT TOUCH

Status: shipped Sprint 4, hardened through Sprint 12. Anything in this section is "read-only, audit-only, do not refactor without `inkos-payments-lead` sign-off."

- **Client:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS/lib/dodo/client.ts` — lazy-init Proxy singleton, never construct at module evaluation time (env vars not loaded yet at build).
- **Webhook:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS/app/api/webhooks/dodo/route.ts` — must follow `standardwebhooks` spec: `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature` headers verified by `timingSafeEqual` (constant-time HMAC), never `===`.
- **Subscription lifecycle handled events:** `subscription.active` / `subscription.cancelled` / `subscription.failed` / `subscription.renewed` / `payment.succeeded` / `payment.failed`. Each event writes to `subscriptions` table via service-role client (bypasses RLS). Web app code is read-only on this table — write-only-by-webhook is locked in CLAUDE.md §7.7.
- **Plan upgrade flow:** `lib/dodo/checkout.ts` builds a Dodo checkout session with `return_url` (NOT `success_url` — gotcha #2 in inkos-lessons §6), customer's `billing.country` is required (ISO-3166 two-letter, gotcha #5).
- **Customer portal:** `lib/dodo/portal.ts` returns `{ link }` from Dodo (NOT `{ url }`, gotcha #3) — embedded in `/settings/billing`.
- **Dunning:** Dodo handles retry schedule + dunning emails; we store `subscription_status` and surface Bone/Stone-tinted banner on `/dashboard` when status ∈ `past_due, paused, cancelled`.
- **Tax:** Dodo is Merchant of Record — they handle global VAT/GST/sales-tax. We never collect tax on the L1 transaction. Receipts come from Dodo, branded as Dodo.

**This stack does not change. The `inkos-payments-lead` agent owns guarding it from regression as Stripe Connect lands.**

### A.2 — L2 (in-studio) Stripe Connect flow — NEW

This is the marketplace layer: studios charge clients for tattoo services, InkOS routes funds with commission splits, tax collection, and 1099 reporting. Stripe Connect Express is the only viable model — full "Custom" KYC is too heavy for an artist who just wants to get paid.

**Recommendation: ONE connected account per studio (Express), commission splits handled in-app via `application_fee_amount`, artist payouts via separate `transfers` API call to per-artist Stripe Express accounts when the artist enables payouts.**

Rationale: simpler KYC for studios (one Express account onboarding), but artists who want direct payouts get their own sub-account so the studio doesn't hold their money beyond the daily cycle. This matches Vagaro/Mindbody mechanics and avoids the W-2 pseudo-employer trap (which a single-pool model would create per IRS ABC test — see compliance section).

**Onboarding flow — studio:**
1. Owner clicks "Enable in-studio payments" in `/settings/payments`.
2. Server creates Stripe Express account: `stripe.accounts.create({ type: 'express', country, capabilities: { card_payments, transfers, tax_reporting_us_1099_nec } })`.
3. Server stores `stripe_connected_accounts` row, returns `account_links.create()` URL → studio redirected to Stripe-hosted KYC.
4. Webhook `account.updated` flips `onboarding_status` from `pending` → `active` when `charges_enabled` and `payouts_enabled` are true.
5. Studio sees Bone/Onyx-tinted banner on `/dashboard` until KYC complete.

**Onboarding flow — artist:**
1. Artist opts in via `/settings/my-payouts`.
2. Server creates a second Express account using `account_links.create()` with the artist's email + TIN/SSN.
3. Webhook `account.updated` flips that artist row's `onboarding_status` to `active`.
4. Until artist completes KYC, their commission accrues to the studio's connected balance and the studio pays them via existing payroll/1099 path.

**Charge flow — exact Stripe call shape (destination charge model):**

```
stripe.paymentIntents.create({
  amount: total_cents,                    // base + tip + tax
  currency: 'usd',
  customer: client_stripe_customer_id,
  payment_method: pm_id,
  confirm: true,
  application_fee_amount: studio_commission_cents,  // 30% in 70/30 split
  transfer_data: { destination: artist_connected_account_id },
  on_behalf_of: artist_connected_account_id,
  automatic_tax: { enabled: true },       // Stripe Tax for US per-state
  metadata: {
    studio_id, artist_id, booking_id, project_id, session_id,
    deposit_pool_drawdown_cents,          // for atomic settlement
    inkos_idempotency_key                 // dedupe in webhook reconciliation
  }
})
```

If the artist hasn't onboarded their own account, `transfer_data.destination` = studio's account, and the studio reconciles internally (artist still gets their share via in-house payroll, no 1099 from Stripe direct).

**Deposit pool charge flow (atomic with new charge):**
- `projects.deposit_pool_cents_available` is the source of truth.
- At session settlement: a Postgres RPC `apply_deposit_to_session(project_id, session_id, draw_cents)` runs in a single transaction:
  1. Verify `available >= draw_cents`.
  2. Decrement `available`, increment `applied`, insert `project_deposit_transactions` row with `kind='applied'`.
  3. The PaymentIntent's `amount` is `(session_total - draw_cents)` — only the balance is charged through Stripe.
  4. If PaymentIntent fails, RPC rolls back (transaction wraps both DB write and external call indirectly via SAGA pattern: write deposit txn as `pending_apply` first, only flip to `applied` on `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook).
- Deposit-only charges (collected at booking creation) hit the studio's connected balance via a charge with NO `transfer_data` — they sit in studio float until applied.

**Tip routing:** Tips are captured in the same PaymentIntent as the session charge (line item `tip_amount_cents`). The `application_fee_amount` excludes the tip, so 100% of tip flows to the artist's `transfer_data.destination`. Studios that pool tips can override this in settings — the override flips the split to: tip goes to studio account, daily transfer cron splits per studio's pool rule.

**Tax line items:** `automatic_tax: { enabled: true }` enables Stripe Tax. Stripe maintains rates for all US states + most EU/CA/AU jurisdictions. For jurisdictions Stripe doesn't cover (e.g., a few rural EU regions, certain tribal-land tattoo taxes), fallback to `tax_rates: [tx_id]` populated manually per location in `/settings/tax`. Tax amount is recorded on the charge metadata AND in `tax_remittance_ledger` for monthly remittance.

**Refund flow:** `stripe.refunds.create({ payment_intent, amount, reverse_transfer: true, refund_application_fee: true })`. `reverse_transfer: true` claws the artist's share back from their connected balance (or debits next payout if balance is insufficient). `refund_application_fee: true` returns the studio's commission portion. We mirror by inserting a `commission_splits` row with `kind='reversal'` and re-incrementing `deposit_pool_cents_available` if the refund originated from pool drawdown.

**Dispute flow:** Webhook on `charge.dispute.created` →
1. Insert `stripe_disputes` row.
2. Enqueue BullMQ job `assemble-dispute-defense-pack`.
3. Job pulls: signed consent form PDF (Sprint 6), photo release PDF, all `project_progress_photos` for the session, conversation thread snapshot from `messages`, deposit policy text, original receipt → bundles into one PDF, uploads to private Storage, stores URL.
4. Submit evidence via `stripe.disputes.update(id, { evidence: { customer_signature, customer_communication, receipt, service_documentation, ... } })` 24h before `evidence_due_by`.
5. If lost: Stripe debits studio's balance; we mirror via a `commission_splits` reversal row clawing artist's share, OR if artist balance is negative, log to `payroll` for next-cycle deduction.

**1099-NEC export:** Annual cron at year-end queries `stripe.transfers.list` per artist's connected account, groups by tax year, exports CSV with `name, TIN/SSN/EIN, federal_id, state_id, total_paid, address` to `/admin/tax-exports`. For studios on the studio-pool model (artist has no own connected account), 1099-NEC is generated from `commission_splits` table directly. Stripe also offers `tax_reporting_us_1099_nec` capability — we enable it on every connected account so Stripe can issue the form too, and we cross-check.

### A.3 — Database schema additions

New tables (Dato writes, all RLS scoped by `studio_id`):

- **`stripe_connected_accounts`** — `id, studio_id, account_id (TEXT, Stripe), type (ENUM studio | artist), artist_id (FK nullable), onboarding_status (pending | active | restricted | rejected), capabilities (JSONB — charges_enabled, payouts_enabled, transfers, tax_reporting), country, default_currency, restricted_reason, requirements_due_by, created_at, updated_at`.
- **`stripe_charges`** — `id, studio_id, payment_intent_id, charge_id, transfer_id, application_fee_id, status, currency, amount_cents, tax_amount_cents, application_fee_cents, net_artist_cents, booking_id (FK), project_id (FK), session_id (FK), client_id (FK), deposit_drawdown_cents, idempotency_key (UNIQUE), created_at`.
- **`stripe_disputes`** — `id, studio_id, dispute_id, charge_id, reason, status, amount_cents, evidence_due_by, defense_pack_url, submission_status (pending | submitted | won | lost), submitted_at, resolved_at, resolved_amount_cents, created_at`.
- **`tax_remittance_ledger`** — `id, studio_id, location_id, jurisdiction (e.g., US-CA, US-NY, EU-DE), period (month/quarter), amount_collected_cents, amount_remitted_cents, remittance_date, remittance_reference, status (open | filed | paid), created_at`.
- **`commission_splits`** — `id, studio_id, booking_id, session_id, artist_id, base_amount_cents, commission_pct (NUMERIC 5,2), tip_amount_cents, applied_from_pool_cents, stripe_transfer_id, kind (split | reversal | adjustment), parent_split_id (for reversals), created_at`.
- **`dispute_defense_packs`** — `id, dispute_id, signed_consent_url, photo_release_url, session_photos_urls (TEXT[]), chat_history_url, deposit_policy_text, receipt_url, bundle_pdf_url, generated_at`.
- **`nec_1099_exports`** — `id, studio_id, year, artist_id, total_paid_cents, federal_id_last4, state_id_last4, csv_url, pdf_url, generated_at, source (stripe | inkos_internal)`.

Schema evolution to existing tables:

- **`bookings`** — ADD `stripe_charge_id, stripe_transfer_id, commission_split_id, tax_amount_cents`.
- **`studios`** — ADD `stripe_connected_account_id, l2_payments_enabled_at`.
- **`artists`** (or `studio_members`) — ADD `stripe_connected_account_id, payouts_self_enabled`.
- **`payments`** (existing Dodo-mirror) — ADD `provider ENUM('dodo' | 'stripe_connect')` to disambiguate L1 vs L2 rows.

### A.4 — Webhook reconciliation

Two webhook sources, one ledger:

- **`webhook_events`** — `id, source ENUM('dodo' | 'stripe'), event_id (UNIQUE on (source, event_id)), event_type, payload JSONB, signature_verified BOOL, processed_at, error TEXT, retry_count INT, created_at`.
- Idempotency: `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (source, event_id) DO NOTHING` is the first write of every webhook handler. If conflict, return 200 immediately.
- Replay protection: Dodo + Stripe both include timestamp headers; reject events older than 5 minutes.
- Audit: every event row keeps full payload for 90 days, then archived.
- **Reconciliation cron (hourly):**
  - For Dodo: list active subscriptions, compare against `subscriptions` table — flag drift.
  - For Stripe: list charges in last 25h, compare against `stripe_charges` — flag drift, log to `/admin/payments/reconciliation` for human review.
- Replay queue: `BullMQ` queue `webhook-replay` per source; failed events auto-retry 3× with exponential backoff (30s, 5m, 1h), then dead-letter for manual.

### A.5 — Failure modes + handling

| Mode | Detection | Handling |
|------|-----------|----------|
| Stripe account `restricted_soon` | `account.updated` webhook | Onyx banner on `/dashboard`, link to KYC. Charges still work. |
| Cross-border charge with FX | PaymentIntent metadata has `presentment_currency` ≠ `settlement_currency` | Record both `amount_cents` (settled) and `presentment_amount_cents` on `stripe_charges`. |
| Dispute lost | `charge.dispute.closed` event with `status='lost'` | Clawback via `commission_splits` reversal; if artist balance negative, log to `payroll` for deduction next cycle. |
| Refund after payout | Refund call returns `requires_action` for transfer reversal | Use `reverse_transfer: true` always; if artist balance positive, instant claw; if negative, debit next payout. |
| Tax remittance failure | Stripe Tax reporting API error | Don't block charge; queue `tax_remittance_ledger` row as `status='manual_review'` for `inkos-compliance-lead` review. |
| Restricted account, charge attempted | Stripe returns `account_invalid` | Bone/Onyx banner blocking checkout, redirect to `/settings/payments/onboarding`. |
| Webhook signature mismatch | `timingSafeEqual` fails | Log to `audit_log`, return 401, alert `inkos-payments-lead` via Hawk. |

## PART B — DATA MODEL EVOLUTION

### B.1 — Sessions as first-class entity

Currently sessions are inferred from `bookings` + `project_progress_photos` slot enums (`s1_fresh`, `s2_healed`, …). PDF treats Session as a project-level event distinct from Booking (a calendar slot).

### B.2 — Persistent allergies banner

`clients.allergies` column exists but has no UI banner. Migrate to:

### B.3 — Client portal magic link

**New table `client_portal_sessions`:** `id, token (UNIQUE), client_id, studio_id, scopes TEXT[], expires_at, used_at, created_at, ip_address (INET), user_agent`.

Token = signed JWT (HS256, secret in env), 15-min expiry. Public route `/portal/[token]` validates via `createPublicClient` (anon Supabase + RPC). RPC `client_portal_get_view(token)` returns project + photos + deposit pool + outstanding forms — all read-only.

**New tables:**
- `ai_drafts` — `id, conversation_id, message_id (FK nullable, set when accepted), draft_text, model, prompt_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_cents, accepted_at, accepted_by, edited_text, created_at`.

### B.8 — Marketing flows

## 1. Context

InkOS is a multi-tenant SaaS replacing the **9 disconnected tools** (Instagram DMs, WhatsApp, email, Google Calendar, Venmo, Stripe, Notes app, Dropbox, group SMS) most tattoo studios glue together. The PDF defines a target product across **three personas** (studio owner Maya, resident artist Miles, client Karisa) walking through a complete **5-session koi sleeve** lifecycle — from first DM through final session through year-later VIP referral.

The product is currently **Sprint 12 complete, launch-ready**: 72 migrations, 511 routes, 286 components, 46 tests. The PDF reveals a **wider target than the existing Sprint 0–12 scope** delivered. This plan closes the gap.

**Why this scope:**
- Yash explicitly requested 50–100 sprints, production-grade, "Lovable-quality" refactor cadence baked in.
- Tax handling has to be best-in-class (MoR for SaaS + per-state line-itemed for in-studio).
